result.summary: The surface of zf 0.11.0, a fuzzy-finder library, consists of a standard Zig build script and manifest. The script exposes the zf module, test steps and an optional TUI executable that uses a hash-pinned, lazily fetched vaxis dependency. I checked for build-time execution, code generation, file reads, network use and unexpected files, found none, and no capabilities were listed to explain.

findings.title: Standard build script
findings.detail: build.zig declares a library module from src/zf/zf.zig, test steps, and an optional TUI executable that depends on the lazily fetched vaxis dependency. It contains no system commands, no build-time code generation, no file reads beyond the source paths and no network access. It does nothing beyond a standard Zig build script.

findings.title: Pinned lazy dependency and restricted package paths
findings.detail: The single dependency is libvaxis, pinned to commit 6fd944a2 with a content hash and marked lazy, so it is fetched only when the TUI is built. The package paths ship only src/zf, the build files and LICENSE, so the src/tui sources the TUI build needs are absent. A consumer importing the zf module therefore gets only the library code.
